solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Liable to have been pelted with rotten veg, thus conk-tip's battered?

definitions.text: Liable to have been pelted with rotten veg, thus conk-tip's battered?

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters before it are knocked into a new order

parts.note: all twelve letters, including the possessive s, are the raw material

explanation.surface: An offender in the village stocks, pelted with rotten vegetables, ends up with a battered nose tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a conk is a nose, and a battered nose is exactly what someone punished in the stocks might get. STOCKPUNISHT is Shakespeare's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-punisht is the old past participle for having been punished in the stocks, where offenders were pelted with refuse.

clue.text: The old wag that could cause annoyance if penning book

indicators.note: the answer would only become the annoying word if it penned, or held, the extra letter, so that letter is missing from the answer

parts.note: to trouble someone is to annoy them
B is the standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A dated joker who, carrying a book, might become a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wag' looks like a joker, but it is a verb: TROULE is an obsolete form of troll, to move the tongue nimbly. Put B into it and you get TROUBLE, which is what could cause annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Troule is an archaic spelling of troll in its old sense of to roll or wag, as a tongue does.

clue.text: Computer group with particular functions maybe approach apparatus

definitions.text: Computer group with particular functions maybe

parts.note: in golf a chip is a short approach shot to the green
a set is an apparatus, as in a television set

explanation.surface: A description of some computing hardware: a group of components designed for particular tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' is the golfing sense, a short lofted shot onto the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipset is a group of integrated circuits designed to work together to perform particular functions in a computer.

clue.text: Film star princess appearing endlessly in film?

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter of the name is cut off

parts.note: Grace Kelly, the Hollywood actress who became Princess of Monaco

explanation.surface: A movie-star royal who seems to be forever on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' appears twice: first as the movies, then at the end as a thin skin, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kell is a dialect word for a caul or thin membrane, which is a film in the sense of a fine covering layer.

clue.text: The old man has bottled beer in this receptacle

definitions.text: The old man has bottled beer in this receptacle

indicators.note: to have something bottled is to hold it enclosed, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Father keeps his bottled beer stored in this container.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a palea is a chaffy scale found on the receptacle of a composite flower, so the 'receptacle' is botanical, not a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a palea is a scale or bract borne on the receptacle of a flower head, so it is something found in this receptacle.

clue.text: Lift ban on exercise involving neuter dog

indicators.note: something that involves other things takes them in, so one word is wrapped round the others

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it
N is the grammatical abbreviation for neuter
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A council lifting a ban on walking a neutered dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neuter' looks like a verb about the dog, but it is the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncurse is to remove a curse, and lifting a ban or interdiction is removing a curse laid on someone.

clue.text: Lake neglected, furious about how it ends, overgrown

indicators.note: about means round, so the shortened word goes round the single letter
something neglected is left out, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: livid means extremely angry
L is the map abbreviation for lake; this is the letter dropped

indicators.note: the way a word ends is its final letter, so only that letter of the lake is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word lake

explanation.surface: An abandoned lake, its owner angry at how it ended up choked with weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake' does two jobs: as L it is dropped from LIVID, and 'how it ends' points back to it for its last letter, E, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied means covered with ivy, so a wall or ruin that is ivied is overgrown with the climber.

clue.text: Salt from America coming up before reprimand

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in the entry
in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: US is the standard abbreviation for the United States
to berate is to scold or reprimand

explanation.surface: An American table salt gets a telling-off before it reaches the shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: A suberate is a salt of suberic acid, the chemist's sense of salt rather than the seasoning.

clue.text: Who's bemused about the whole bang shoot? Bless!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the muddled word goes round the other
a bemused person is muddled, so the letters of the word are muddled into a new order

parts.note: the word who, with the 's standing for 'is'
the whole bang shoot is a slang phrase for everything, all of it

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by the whole business throws up their hands with an exasperated exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bless!' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but it is the plain verb, to bless.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallow is to make holy or consecrate, which is to bless something.

clue.text: Amateur music society, English, going into wards, often?

indicators.note: going into puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a ward of court is often a child without parents
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An amateur music society taking an English group into the care of hospital wards.
explanation.walkthrough: Wards here are children under guardianship, not hospital rooms; the question mark admits that wards are only often orphans.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheans, named after Orpheus the mythical musician, is a traditional name for an amateur choral or music society.

clue.text: Nick Compton's opener featuring in varied Lord's chat (10, two words)

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear inside it
something varied has been changed, so these letters come in a changed order

parts.note: all nine letters are reworked

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: the first letter of Compton

explanation.surface: Cricket chat: Nick Compton opening the batting is discussed in the commentary box at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Compton is a real England opening batsman, and Lord's is the London cricket ground, but 'Nick' is the definition: Old Nick, the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Scratch and Old Nick are both folk nicknames for the Devil, so one stands for the other.

clue.text: Edward aboard his bathyscape? It's in the blood

definitions.note: a phrase describing something deep-seated; the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: being aboard places the person with the vessel, so one piece directly follows the other

parts.note: a bathyscape is a submersible craft for exploring the deep sea
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward on board his own deep-diving submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: DEEP SEA plus TED reads as a deep-sea Ted, a man aboard his bathyscape. The answer is the single word DEEPSEATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deep-seated is firmly fixed and ingrained, like a trait people say is in the blood.

clue.text: Extract from Annal of India not particularly well reproduced

indicators.note: an extract is a piece taken out of a longer text, so the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of annal, all of of, and the start of India

explanation.surface: A passage from a historical chronicle of India, poorly copied.
explanation.walkthrough: LO-FI is short for low fidelity, the opposite of hi-fi.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo-fi sound is low fidelity, recorded or played back with deliberately unpolished quality.

clue.text: Bone left in Church, riddled?

indicators.note: in places the bone and the side inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a rib is a bone
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A bone discovered in a church, which turns out to be full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIBLE is a term from engraving for a surface dotted with small punched holes; the question mark flags that sense of 'riddled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crible describes metal or wood engraved with many small dots or holes, as if riddled with them like a sieve.

clue.text: Shape for cooking the French put on counter

indicators.note: in an across entry one piece put on another is placed after it

parts.note: a dump is an old word for a small counter or token used in games
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A cook shaping food on a kitchen counter, French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' suggests a worktop, but it is a token: a dump, a small lead counter once used by children in games.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumple is to shape something into a dumpling, ready for cooking.

clue.text: Old sewer? Not old when fish is found in it

indicators.note: when the fish is found in it, the archaic word holds the fish inside

parts.note: ne is an archaic word for not
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An old drain that turns out not to be old after all, since there are fish living in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A sewer here is something that sews, and 'Not old' means the old word for not, not 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neele is an obsolete spelling of needle, the tool used by anyone who sews.

clue.text: Some primates, old-maidish about bits of obscene speech I repeated

indicators.note: about means around, so the prim word is wrapped round the selected letters

parts.note: prim, stiffly proper, is what an old-maidish person is

indicators.note: bits of a phrase are small pieces of it, here the first letter of each word

parts.note: the first letters of obscene and speech
the letter I twice

explanation.surface: A prudish observer recoils at some apes using coarse language.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosimii is the zoological name for the prosimians, the lemurs, lorises and their kin, a group of primates.

clue.text: Feature of e.g. Arnhem road damaged in blast

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other word

parts.note: a parp is a blast on a horn

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word road

explanation.surface: A wartime road at Arnhem wrecked by an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnhem was the 1944 battle in which Allied troops were landed by parachute behind enemy lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradrop is a delivery of troops or supplies by parachute, the defining tactic of the Arnhem operation.

clue.text: Minor planet, dry and cold when viewed from behind

indicators.note: viewing something from behind means reading it from its far end, right to left

parts.note: sere means dried up or withered
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes a small planet as dry and cold, seen from its far side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres, in the asteroid belt, was the first asteroid discovered and is now classed as a dwarf planet, a minor planet.

clue.text: Gaiety e.g. as mad Hatter grabs dormouse's tail

indicators.note: to grab something is to take hold of it, so the rearranged word encloses the single letter
something mad is crazed and disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word Hatter

indicators.note: a tail is the hindmost part, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of dormouse

explanation.surface: A scene from Alice in Wonderland at the tea party: the Mad Hatter grabs the Dormouse by the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gaiety was a famous London playhouse, so it is one example of a theatre; 'Gaiety' is not cheerfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaiety, a well-known London playhouse of the Victorian and Edwardian era, is an example of a theatre.

clue.text: Spy dropping out acquires unprepared bit if thin turf

indicators.note: acquiring something adds it on, so the next piece is joined to the shortened word
dropping something leaves it behind, so these letters go

parts.note: a scout is someone sent to spy out the land
the word out itself, removed
raw means unready or unprepared, as with an untrained recruit

explanation.surface: A dropped-out spy picks up some odd scrap of thin turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If' in the definition is a slip for 'of': a bit of thin turf. Scraw is an Irish and Scottish word for a sod of turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A scraw is a thin sod or strip of turf, especially as cut for roofing in Ireland and Scotland.

clue.text: Switches part of current account put into reserve funds

indicators.note: putting something into something else places it inside

parts.note: in banking a rest is a reserve fund
C/A is the bank abbreviation for a current account

explanation.surface: A customer moves part of their current account into their savings reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switches part' looks like money being moved, but it means a director giving a role to a new actor; a current account is the British name for a checking account.
explanation.definitionFit: A director who recasts gives a role to a different actor, switching who plays the part.

clue.text: Central heating working properly when on, making Scots fidget

parts.note: central heating that works properly is hot when it is switched on
CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: When the heating finally works, the Scottish household can't sit still.
explanation.walkthrough: The heating is CH, and how it should be when on, HOT, comes first. HOTCH is a Scots verb, to fidget or jerk about.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, to hotch is to fidget or move restlessly, so it is the Scots word for fidget.

clue.text: E.g. dynamite blasted iron junk?

parts.note: dynamite is an example of a high explosive, HE

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word iron

explanation.surface: Dynamite used to blow up old scrap iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' looks like scrap metal after 'iron', but it is drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk is street slang for heroin, and a junkie is an addict.

clue.text: Meat preservative? Portion of tripe treated

indicators.note: a portion is part of a whole, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of tripe and the start of treated

explanation.surface: A cook asks what keeps meat fresh, given a portion of processed tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: Petre is a short form of saltpetre, long used to cure meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Petre, short for saltpetre or potassium nitrate, has long been used as a curing agent to preserve meat.

clue.text: Might it be synonymous with 'sublingual', artist muses?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
the Muses of Greek myth were nine sisters

explanation.surface: An artist idly wondering whether two anatomical words mean the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muses' is not a verb for the artist pondering: it is the Nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranine describes the underside of the tongue, the region a sublingual vein lies in, so the two terms overlap in anatomy.

clue.text: After the tide turns, former drudge becomes …

definitions.note: the ellipsis runs on to 28-across, whose opening words, One absorbed by arts, define this answer

indicators.note: after signals that the next piece follows the first in the entry
turning something round makes it face the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: tide is a poetic word for the sea
a thete was a labourer of the lowest free class in ancient Athens

explanation.surface: When the tide turns, a one-time drudge transforms into something new.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the next clue: 'becomes …' leads to 'One absorbed by arts' at 28-across, which is also part of that clue's wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone devoted to beauty and the arts, a person absorbed by them.

clue.text: Gettin' the measure of a simple putt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ...', measuring with a tape, with the final g dropped as the clue's spelling shows
second meaning: a very short putt in golf that is simply tapped in

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Gettin'' is the signal: the first meaning also drops its g. The answer is TAP-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-in is a golf putt so short it is just tapped into the hole, and tapin' is a casual spelling of taping, measuring.

clue.text: What pipe cleaner clears round half of bowl — something you get with a pipe

definitions.text: something you get with a pipe

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: a pipe cleaner clears tar from a tobacco pipe
the first half of the word bowl

explanation.surface: A smoker's routine: the pipe cleaner scraping out the bowl of a tobacco pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The pipe changes meaning: first a tobacco pipe, then the musical pipe, which in folk music was traditionally played with a small drum in the other hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabor is a small drum traditionally played by one musician together with a pipe, as in pipe and tabor.

clue.text: … One absorbed by arts, adrift in 'rock period'?

indicators.note: to be absorbed by something is to be taken inside it
something adrift has broken loose, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word arts
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone lost in the arts, drifting through a rock music era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock period' suggests a phase of rock music; geologically it is the Triassic. The words 'One absorbed by arts' also define 25-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Trias is an older name for the Triassic, a geological period identified by its characteristic rock strata.

clue.text: Acting against gossip from the past, the old move on

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acting, as in A/Manager
v is the abbreviation for versus, against
aunt in an old sense means a gossip or old woman

explanation.surface: Turning against old gossip, the elderly residents move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks the definition as archaic: avaunt is a dated command meaning be gone, move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an archaic interjection ordering someone to go away, the old way of saying move on.

clue.text: Climber from Argentina getting lost at head of gorge

indicators.note: these letters disappear from the front of the next word, its head

parts.note: a ravine is a narrow gorge
RA is the international vehicle code for Argentina

explanation.surface: A mountaineer from Argentina goes missing at the top of a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' wants to be a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A vine is a plant that climbs by tendrils or twining stems, so it is a climber.

clue.text: Count no longer fed with duck or fruit pudding

indicators.note: something fed with another thing takes it inside

parts.note: compt is an obsolete spelling of count
in cricket a duck is a score of zero, O

explanation.surface: A deposed count no longer fed on duck, but given fruit pudding instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count no longer' looks like a nobleman who lost his title; it means a word for count no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: A compot, or compote, is fruit stewed in syrup and served as a dessert.

clue.text: Old mount is obliging, moving rear to the front

indicators.note: taking the last letter and putting it first rotates the word by one place

parts.note: someone who ties another is obliging, or binding, them

explanation.surface: A horse from long ago, kind enough to let the rider shuffle forward from its rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' is a verb, to climb: STIE is an old spelling of sty, to ascend.
explanation.definitionFit: Stie, an obsolete form of sty, means to climb or ascend, an old word for mount.

clue.text: X inscribed in leaf — it involves interaction with the public

definitions.text: it involves interaction with the public

indicators.note: something inscribed in a surface is written inside it

parts.note: a frond is a large leaf, as of a fern or palm
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A kiss written on a leaf, presumably a public declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like a kiss or a mark, but it is the Roman ten. FRONT END is the customer-facing part of a business or system.
explanation.definitionFit: The front end of a business or software system is the part that deals directly with customers or users, the public face.

clue.text: En suite trend transformed, rendering one apathetic?

indicators.note: something transformed is changed in form, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: all twelve letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The fashion for en suite bathrooms has made someone indifferent to home design.
explanation.walkthrough: An en suite is a bathroom attached to a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninterested shows no interest or concern, which is to be apathetic.
